approach:
Catalyst-triggered, fundamentally-filtered, sector-capped concentrated screen — run live, never backtested end-to-end.

The trigger is NSE's canonical filing subject "Bagging/Receiving of orders/contracts", NOT the repo's `orders` regex category. This is the largest change my inspection forced. Of the 14,923 filings the classifier tags as `orders`, only 2,384 (16%) carry that canonical subject. 3,357 (22.5%) are "Action(s) initiated or orders passed" — SEBI and regulatory ENFORCEMENT actions. Another 776 are GST demand orders and tax assessment orders. Roughly a quarter of the archive's best-scoring bullish signal is bad news, swept in because the regex matches \border(s)?\b. Verified by eye: "Action(s) initiated or orders passed: Suumaya Industries", "GST Demand Order - Fenesta" (DCM Shriram), "rectification of assessment order passed by Navi Mumbai Municipal Corporation" (Thyrocare) are all currently classified as order wins.

Pipeline: canonical order-win filing in the last 20 sessions → six binary hard filters (any failure is fatal, ranking never rescues) → composite rank on sector-relative valuation and returns on capital → hand-assigned sector buckets cap it at 3 per bucket → top 10 → buy next open in one tranche → exits written into the order at entry.

Fundamentals filter, they do not rank the trigger. Price data ranks nothing. Volume appears nowhere.
thesis: An order win is a contracted future cash flow from a named counterparty — the least ambiguous good news an Indian company can file, verifiable, and about forward revenue rather than the past. The repo's own study measured it beating Nifty 500 at 63.2% over 12 months against a 43.3% random baseline (z = +13.4, n = 2,379), with the effect strengthening to 24 months. Fundamentals cannot generate that signal — three balance-sheet dates cannot rank anything — but they can veto it. The failure mode of a catalyst strategy is buying a genuine order win at a leveraged, loss-making, over-priced company that dilutes or defaults before the contract converts to cash; the event study's own worst-case column shows -94% outcomes inside the winning sample. So the catalyst supplies the timing and the direction, the fundamentals supply the survival screen, and the sector-appropriate multiple supplies the price discipline. The Rs 50k position size is what makes this workable at all: the canonical trigger fires on ~240 symbols a year, most of them small caps no institution can size into, and at 0.05% of daily turnover his impact cost is zero where theirs is prohibitive.
hard_filters: CATALYST: a filing whose subject begins 'Bagging/Receiving of orders/contracts', with trade_date within the last 20 trading sessions. Not the `orders` regex category — that bucket is 22.5% regulatory enforcement actions and 5% tax demands.

LIQUIDITY: median daily turnover over the trailing 60 sessions >= Rs 1 crore. At Rs 50k a position that is ~0.05% of a day's trade, so impact cost is nil on entry AND on exit — the exit is the half that matters, because a pre-committed stop is worthless in a name he cannot sell. 494 of the 607 symbols with a 2026 order filing clear this.

LEVERAGE: debt_to_equity <= 1.5 from the most recent filing where has_balance_sheet is true. ABSENCE IS A REJECT, not a pass — debt_to_equity is populated on only 44.6% of financials rows overall (91.7% of balance-sheet rows), and a missing denominator is exactly how a levered company slips through.

INTEREST COVER: ebitda / finance_costs >= 3 on the most recent quarter. This is the leverage cap's teeth. D/E comes from a balance sheet that may be 12-18 months old; interest cover is available every quarter and is current. A company that levered up since September 2025 shows it here first.

EARNINGS QUALITY: profit_normalised > 0 in each of the two most recent available quarters. Sign-based, no coefficient — the test is that stripping exceptional items does not turn the profit into a loss. Uses profit_normalised, not profit_reported, so a land sale cannot buy a place on the shortlist.

NOT ALREADY RE-RATED: measured from the close the session before the filing to the current close, the move is greater than 0% and less than +15%. Measured on 2022-23 order events: the >15% bucket beat the benchmark 61.1% of the time versus 65.3% for the +2-6% bucket, and the sub-zero bucket collapsed to 49.3% with -1.0% median excess. A big gap says the news is already in the price; a negative reaction says the market read the filing and did not believe it.

EXCLUDE BANKS, NBFCs AND INSURERS ENTIRELY. Leverage is their business model, so a D/E cap of 1.5 is structurally unsatisfiable; EBITDA is meaningless; and the financials table holds no adjusted book value, no GNPA, no provision coverage. His own rule says value them on P/Adjusted-BV — the data cannot compute it, so they are out rather than mis-screened.
ranking_factors: Sector-relative valuation percentile, cheaper ranks better. The multiple is chosen by the hand-assigned sector bucket per his own rules: P/E for asset-light and stable (IT services, mature consumer, pharma), EV/EBITDA for capital-intensive (construction, engineering, cement, steel, power, telecom, shipping, hotels). Percentile is computed WITHIN the bucket against every screened peer, never against the whole market — a construction company on 18x EV/EBITDA and an IT company on 18x P/E are not comparable and ranking them on one axis is the classic way a screen ends up long only the cheapest sector.

Return on capital employed, higher ranks better, against his 12% hurdle. Computed as annualised EBIT / (assets - current_liabilities) from the latest half-yearly balance sheet. Crude — see data_we_lack — but it is the only capital-efficiency read available and a below-12% ROCE on an order-driven capex story is the signal that the order will consume more capital than it returns.

Smallness: market cap below Rs 5,000 crore ranks ahead. Not because small is better in itself but because that is where his Rs 50k size stops being a limitation and starts being access to names institutions cannot touch. Market cap = current close x (equity_capital / face_value), NOT close x shares_implied — see data_we_lack.

Revenue growth, latest quarter versus the prior quarter, higher ranks better. Sequential, not year-on-year, because no symbol in the table has four quarters. This factor is the weakest of the four and is knowingly seasonally contaminated for exactly the construction and capital-goods names the trigger over-selects.

Composite = equal-weighted average of whichever ranks are computable for that name. Equal weights are a refusal to fit, not a judgement. Any weighting scheme would add four more parameters to tune on a dataset that cannot validate them.
entry_rule:
Buy at the next session's open after the name clears every hard filter and lands in the top 10 of the composite rank, one tranche, the full Rs 50k. No scaling in, no waiting for a pullback — waiting for a better price is where his impatience gets its entry point, and a rule that permits deliberation reintroduces the failure mode the system exists to remove. If a name qualifies but its sector bucket already holds 3 positions it is skipped permanently, not queued.

On "entry BEFORE a rally", he must hear this plainly, because the data contradicts the instruction as stated. I tested it directly: 2,386 order-win events from 2022-23, split into quartiles by the stock's trailing 3-month return measured strictly before the filing date. Buying the coldest quartile — the unloved names that had not moved, which is what "before a rally" literally means — produced a 51.8% beat rate and +2.2% median excess. The hottest quartile produced 64.7% and +18.7%. On trailing 12-month return the spread is worse: 54.9% versus 74.4%. The relationship is monotonic across all four quartiles in both cases. Filtering for names that have not yet run would have destroyed roughly two-thirds of the edge and left him barely above the random baseline.

So the rule implements the defensible version of his intent and refuses the literal one. The rally he is trying to get in front of is the 12-24 month re-rating that the order converts into earnings, not the last quarter's price action. Filter 6 is what enforces "before": it rejects a stock that has already jumped more than 15% on THIS filing. It does not reject a stock that has been doing well. He should decide whether he accepts that substitution with the numbers in front of him, because it is the single largest departure from his stated preference in this design, and the evidence for it is one bull-market regime.
exit_rules: TIME: exit at 18 months from entry. A fresh canonical order-win filing arriving in the final 6 months resets the clock once and only once, to a hard maximum of 30 months. The 24-month event-study row is stronger than the 12-month row, which is why the horizon is long; the single reset is why it is not open-ended.

STOP: exit if the position closes 25% below entry on any session. No exceptions, no averaging down, no 'it is a good company at a better price'. Averaging down is the mechanical form of the behaviour he described.

THESIS BREAK, exit within 2 sessions, detected from the announcements feed itself: a credit rating downgrade filing, a pledge filing showing an increase, an auditor resignation, a promoter-group stake sale, or any disclosure that the order was cancelled, curtailed or terminated. These are the events that make the reason for owning the stock untrue.
LEVERAGE BREAK: exit at the next half-yearly balance sheet if debt_to_equity crosses 1.5, or if interest cover falls below 2 in any quarter. The entry condition failing is an exit condition.

NO PROFIT TARGET, deliberately. The measured edge strengthens from 12 to 24 months, so a target would cut the winners short — which is the mirror image of his failure mode and just as expensive. The four rules above are the only exits, and none of them is a decision made in the moment.

OPERATIONAL: all of these must be standing orders or a daily automated check that produces an instruction, not a note he intends to act on. A pre-committed exit that requires him to choose to obey it on the day is not pre-committed. This is the only part of the design that has nothing to do with data and everything to do with whether the system survives its first 30% drawdown.
data_we_lack: THE CLEAN TRIGGER HAS NEVER BEEN MEASURED. NSE's canonical 'Bagging/Receiving of orders/contracts' subject appears only from 2024 (181 filings in 2024, 1,120 in 2025, 1,083 in 2026) — NSE changed its subject taxonomy. There are ZERO canonical labels in 2022-23, which is the exact window that produced the 63.2% beat rate. So the signal I am proposing to trade and the signal that was measured are different populations. Contamination with regulatory and tax orders would bias the measured number DOWN, so the clean signal is plausibly stronger — but that is a guess, and it is not evidence.

FUNDAMENTALS ARE STALE, NOT LIVE. Latest period_end in the financials parquet is 2025-09-30 and the latest broadcast_dt is 2025-11-06. Today is 2026-09-08. Every fundamental filter in this design would currently run on data up to twelve months old. Worse, the parquet mirror is behind the locked DuckDB: 7,851 rows in parquet versus 10,348 in the database per financials.log, whose last chunk covers 2025-12-08 to 2026-01-07. This is NOT a live screen until that backfill completes and the mirror is rewritten. That is the single largest blocker to running this at all.

TWO BALANCE-SHEET DATES, NOT THREE. Only 2025-03-31 and 2025-09-30 carry has_balance_sheet; 2025-06-30 has it on 28 of 3,825 rows. And the September file covers roughly half of March's universe (817 standalone / 630 consolidated versus 1,464 / 1,115), so for a large fraction of names the only available D/E is from March 2025 — eighteen months old.

NO TTM EARNINGS. Maximum three quarters exist per symbol (1,079 symbols have 3, 568 have 2, 58 have 1). Trailing-twelve-month EPS cannot be computed for anyone. P/E must be built from an annualised single quarter, which is seasonally wrong for construction, cement, sugar and capital goods — precisely the sectors the order-win trigger over-selects. Year-on-year revenue growth is impossible for the same reason.

shares_implied IS UNRELIABLE AND MUST NOT BE USED. It is derived as profit / EPS, which breaks for consolidated entities with minority interests. Measured: GRASIM 176 crore shares against an actual ~68 crore; BAJAJFINSV 336 crore against ~159 crore; ADANIPOWER 1,900 crore against ~385 crore. Market caps built on it are wrong by 2-5x on exactly the conglomerate names. The working substitute is equity_capital / face_value, with face value joined from universe.json on scrip_id — I verified this reproduces BSE market cap within ~0.2% on RELIANCE, LT, TCS, MARUTI and INFY. But that join is NSE symbol to BSE scrip_id and is unverified across the long tail, which is where this screen actually operates.

NO USABLE SECTOR FIELD. announcements.industry is NULL on 60% of order filings, and only 259 of the 634 symbols with a 2026 order filing carry an industry on ANY filing ever. universe.json's INDUSTRY column is null throughout. The 3-per-sector cap and the choice of P/E versus EV/EBITDA therefore have to be assigned BY HAND on a shortlist of 20-40 names. That is feasible at this scale and I would rather say so than automate a mapping that covers 40% of the universe.

NO PROMOTER PLEDGE PERCENTAGE. Anywhere. There is a `pledge` announcement category, but it records that a filing happened, not what fraction of the promoter holding is encumbered. His hard limit — pledging low or clearly justified — CANNOT be enforced from this data. It requires a manual NSDL or BSE shareholding-pattern check on each of the ten names before buying, and there is no substitute.
NO CASH BALANCE. Not a tagged field. EV can only be market cap plus debt_total, which overstates enterprise value for every cash-rich company and systematically penalises them in the EV/EBITDA rank.

ROCE IS AN ESTIMATE, NOT A MEASUREMENT. Capital employed is only computable as assets minus current_liabilities on the two half-yearly dates, and EBIT has to be backed out of ebitda minus depreciation with other_income sitting in an ambiguous position. Against a 12% hurdle, the estimation error is a material fraction of the thing being measured.

NO ORDER VALUE. I checked: not one of the 14,923 order filings carries a rupee amount in the subject line. The screen cannot distinguish a Rs 5 crore order from a Rs 5,000 crore one, or know what fraction of annual revenue it represents. That is almost certainly the strongest available refinement to this entire design — order value as a percentage of trailing revenue — and it requires parsing the filing PDFs, which nobody has done.

THE ANNOUNCEMENT ARCHIVE HAS A HOLE. No filings at all for 2026-05, 2026-06 or 2026-07, and partial coverage in 2026-04 (192 order filings against a ~400 monthly norm), 2026-08 (80) and 2026-09 (72). The trigger feed is not current and a screen run today would be blind to four of the last five months.

ONE REGIME, AND AN EXTRAORDINARY ONE. Every number here comes from 2022-23, when the RANDOM baseline itself returned +22.1% median over 24 months. Whether order wins work in a flat or falling market is untested and untestable until the archive extends further back. The repo's own study calls this its single largest caveat and nothing I found changes that.
data_required: announcements: subject, trade_date, an_dt, symbol — filtered on subject LIKE 'Bagging/Receiving of orders/contracts%', not on category='orders'
announcements: category and subject for the thesis-break exit watchlist (ratings downgrades, pledge increases, auditor resignations, promoter stake sales, order cancellations)
prices: date, symbol, series, close, turnover — for the liquidity floor, the pre-entry move test, market cap, and the -25% stop
corpactions: symbol, ex_date, factor — split and bonus adjustment, via zen.validation.eventstudy.adjusted_prices
financials: debt_to_equity, debt_total, equity, has_balance_sheet, period_end, broadcast_dt (point-in-time, never period_end)
financials: ebitda, finance_costs, depreciation, profit_normalised, profit_reported, revenue, eps_basic
universe.json: FACE_VALUE and scrip_id — the only reliable path to a share count
indices: Nifty 500 daily close, as the benchmark every result is read against
MANUAL, per shortlist name and unavoidable: sector bucket assignment, and the promoter pledge percentage from NSDL or the BSE shareholding pattern
sector_handling:
Hand-assigned buckets, because the data gives no alternative — `industry` is null on 60% of order filings and on 375 of the 634 symbols with a 2026 order filing.

Roughly ten buckets, each carrying its own valuation multiple: Construction & Infrastructure (EV/EBITDA), Capital Goods & Engineering (EV/EBITDA), Defence & Electronics (EV/EBITDA), Power & Utilities (EV/EBITDA), Metals & Materials incl. cement and steel (EV/EBITDA), Chemicals (EV/EBITDA), Auto & Ancillaries (P/E), Pharma & Healthcare (P/E), IT Services (P/E), Consumer (P/E). Financials get no bucket because they are excluded outright.

Maximum 3 per bucket, 4 only on his explicit override. The cap is applied at selection: a qualifying name whose bucket is full is dropped, never queued.

The blunt problem with this, which the cap does not solve: order wins concentrate overwhelmingly in one macro trade. In the 2025-26 order filings the top industries are Construction (366 filings, 45 symbols), Engineering (187), Electrical Equipment (106), Cement (86), Industrial Electronics (83), Steel (64), Transmission Towers (33). Construction, Engineering, Electrical Equipment, Transmission Towers and Defence are five buckets and one bet — Indian government and utility capex. A portfolio of ten names spread across "different sectors" under this cap could still be a single undiversified position on the capex cycle. He should read the sector cap as controlling stock-specific blow-ups, which it does well, and NOT as controlling factor risk, which it barely touches. If he wants the second thing, the honest instrument is a limit on total capex-cycle exposure across buckets — say no more than 5 of 10 — imposed as a judgement, since no data here can calibrate it.
how_it_could_fail:
"The most likely failure is that the whole edge was 2022-23 small-cap beta. The random baseline in that window returned +22.1% median over 24 months; every category in the study looked positive because the market was. If 2026-28 is flat, order-win names may simply get the median stock's fate — and the repo already established that the median liquid Indian stock LAGS Nifty 500, with only 42.6% beating it over 12 months.

The second failure is that I am trading a signal nobody has measured. The 63.2% came from a 2022-23 sample in which 22.5% of the events were regulatory enforcement actions and 5% were tax demands, misclassified as order wins by a regex matching \border(s)?\b. My clean trigger — NSE's canonical subject line — exists only from 2024, so the measured signal and the traded signal cannot be the same population, and the clean one has zero out-of-sample evidence. The contamination was bad news scored as good, so cleaning it should help, but 'should' is not a result.

The third is that the fundamental filters are theatre. They run on balance sheets up to eighteen months old, from a parquet mirror 2,500 rows behind the database, with no pledge data at all. A company can lever past 1.5, lose its auditor and pledge the promoter stake inside that window and still pass. Interest cover is the only current read and it is one quarter of one ratio.

The fourth is concentration. Ten names on Rs 5 lakh is 10% per position, and the worst 12-month outcome inside the winning order-win sample was -94%. The -25% stop is the only defence, and stops gap through in thin Indian small caps — the exit can easily print at -40%.

The fifth is the one that actually ends strategies: he overrides a rule once. The 18-month clock and the -25% stop will collide during a drawdown, which is precisely the moment his stated failure mode activates. If the exits are notes rather than standing instructions, this design has no mechanism at all and is just a stock list.

And the honest structural point: this design cannot be validated. Only 5 of its 6 parameters touch price data, and those can only be tested on 2024-26 canonical filings — about two years, one regime, with 12-month outcomes complete for barely the 2024-25 subset. The fundamental filters and the ROCE hurdle will never be backtested with this data. The trial log already stands at 15; the one-at-a-time grid below adds 17, so any Sharpe must be deflated against ~32 trials, not against one. Grid, deliberately narrow and one-at-a-time around the priors rather than a 162-cell cross product: turnover floor {0.5, 1, 2 cr}; catalyst window {10, 20, 40 sessions}; max pre-entry move {+10%, +15%, +25%}; hold horizon {12, 18, 24 months}; stop {-20%, -25%, -30%}; interest cover {2, 3}."
